key_insight: MSVR extends variance reduction to track many coupled inner functions with only one or a few stochastic block probes per step, enabling efficient optimization for finite-sum compositional problems.
engineering_relevance: This matters for large-scale machine learning systems where inner-model evaluations are expensive or partially observable, improving sample efficiency without requiring full access to all components each iteration.
method: Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) estimator for partial block tracking.
Algorithms for FCCO under non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
Improved dependence on m when outer gradients are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample complexity guarantees across multiple objective classes and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate stochastic block sampling and estimator stability; practical gains may weaken if block access is highly noisy or poorly balanced.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
